name: Lavender
short: A large review found a safe profile in trials but poor safety reporting. Case reports link continuous use of lavender-fragranced products to breast growth in young children, reversing on stopping.
text: A systematic review and meta-analysis of lavender for anxiety (65 randomised trials, 7993 participants, covering inhaled, oral and massage use) concluded that the available information outlines a safe profile for lavender-based interventions, while noting that most trials had a high risk of bias and that safety data need to be collected and reported more carefully. Case reports describe three prepubertal girls and one boy with breast growth and a history of continuous exposure to lavender-containing fragrances (not oral supplements); the breast growth went away after the products were stopped, and the authors stated that it is unknown whether the oestrogen-like potency of lavender oil is sufficient to cause these effects. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
